title: Module 1 quiz — Enterprise Java Engineering
description: Eight questions on the JDK/JVM, SOLID and the BayPay domain model, collections, exceptions, and enterprise write practices. All names and amounts are synthetic.

questions.prompt: A BayPay JAR compiled with javac --release 21 fails on a laptop with UnsupportedClassVersionError: class file version 65.0. What is the first fix?
choices: Rewrite Money to avoid BigDecimal so the class file is smaller
Run the process on a JDK 21 JVM (or point JAVA_HOME at 21)
Add --enable-preview to the laptop java command
Downgrade Spring Boot so it emits Java 8 bytecode
questions.explanation: Major 65 is Java 21 bytecode. An older JVM cannot load it. Change the runtime (or JAVA_HOME) first. Preview flags and framework downgrades do not address a class-file version mismatch.

questions.prompt: Which SOLID mapping is correct for BayPay?
choices: S: Payment sends the completion email; O: each new status needs a new if in every controller
S: Payment does not send email; O: new legal edges live in allowedNext(); D: the service depends on PaymentAuthorizer
L: a test double that always approves a frozen account is acceptable because tests should be fast
D: the service constructs a concrete card-network SDK so integration tests stay realistic
questions.explanation: SOLID: one reason to change (Payment is not a notifier), extend edges in allowedNext(), depend on PaymentAuthorizer. An always-approve double violates Liskov; a concrete SDK in the service violates Dependency Inversion. Money still rejects zero in its constructor.

choices: RECEIVED → VALIDATING
VALIDATING → DECLINED
RECEIVED → COMPLETED
COMPLETED → REVERSED
questions.explanation: The happy path is RECEIVED → VALIDATING → AUTHORIZED → PROCESSING → COMPLETED. Skipping authorization is an illegal edge. DECLINED from VALIDATING and REVERSED from COMPLETED are documented.

questions.prompt: You need allowedNext() for eight PaymentStatus values. Which collection is the best default?
choices: List<String> of status names so product can add statuses in a database row
Hashtable<PaymentStatus, PaymentStatus>
EnumSet of PaymentStatus (or an EnumMap table of EnumSets)
Raw List so erasure is explicit
questions.explanation: A closed enum universe belongs in EnumSet. String lists accept typos; Hashtable is a synchronized leftover; raw lists erase type safety.

questions.prompt: Avery Chen’s frozen account (22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222) is used with a valid 25.00 USD. What should the validator do?
choices: Throw CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND because frozen customers are deleted
Return a decline decision (account is not ACTIVE) and allow a DECLINED payment
Return Optional.empty() and let the controller invent a 404
Catch Exception and return true so the ledger can sort it out
questions.explanation: The request is interpretable. Authorization refuses a non-ACTIVE account. That is a Decision.decline, then payment.decline, not a missing customer and not a swallowed success.

questions.prompt: Why is accounts.findById(id).orElse(null) a production defect in payment creation?
choices: Optional cannot hold JPA entities
It reintroduces null so a missing account becomes an NPE or a skipped ownership check instead of ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND
orElse(null) is slower than get()
BayPay forbids Optional on repository methods
questions.explanation: Optional means the lookup may miss. orElse(null) throws away that information. The next field access NPEs or, worse, skips belongsTo. Use orElseThrow with a domain error.

questions.prompt: A client retries POST /api/v1/payments with the same Idempotency-Key and a different amount. What must BayPay return?
choices: The original payment as a silent replay so the client is not confused
A second COMPLETED payment because amounts differ
IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (409): same key, different canonical body
200 with an empty body because retries are ignored
questions.explanation: Replay requires the same key and the same body hash. A different amount is a conflict. Silent replay would report the old amount as if the new one posted.

questions.prompt: Money.equals should use which comparison, and why?
choices: amount.equals(other.amount), because scale is part of the legal tender definition
amount.compareTo(other.amount) == 0, so 10.0 USD and 10.00 USD are the same value
Double.compare(amount.doubleValue(), other.amount.doubleValue()) for speed
System.identityHashCode, because each Money construction is unique
questions.explanation: BigDecimal.equals is scale-sensitive. Payments care about numeric value. compareTo plus a hashCode that uses stripTrailingZeros keeps Set/Map keys honest. double is not money; identity is for entities, not values.
